The native CSV reader, which requires the extension. See Reading CSV files for options, types, missing values, and errors.

Reading a file

read_csv()

Read a delimited text file the way phibble’s PHP reader (after readr::read_delim()) does: same records, names, guessed types, values and problem messages. Contract and phibble/readr differences: docs/io.qmd. Dates are int days since 1970-01-01; datetimes are int microseconds since the epoch (UTC); NA is null. failed counts values that did not parse under the column’s type (they are null). Skipped (’_’) columns are null.

Phit\read_csv(    string $path,    array $options = [],): array
Parameter Type Default Description
$path string required A readable file (bytes are passed through; no encoding validation)
$options array [] readr’s defaults when omitted

Returns array{names: list<string>, columns: list<null\|array{type: 'bool'\|'int'\|'float'\|'string'\|'date'\|'datetime', values: list<bool\|int\|float\|string\|null>, failed: int}>, problems: list<string>}

Errors Missing or unreadable file, or an invalid option.

See also Details

Reading in chunks

CsvReader

Reads a CSV file a chunk of rows at a time, as phibble’s DataFrame::csvChunks() (after readr::read_delim_chunked()): only the current chunk is held. Options are read_csv()’s; types not given are guessed from the first chunk (guess_max of its rows) and every later chunk is parsed as those types. Problem rows are numbered from the start of the file.

CsvReader::__construct()

Opens the file and reads its header line.

public function __construct(string $path, array $options = [])
Parameter Description
$path A readable file
$options

Errors Missing or unreadable file, or an invalid option.

CsvReader::names()

Column names: the header’s, or X1..Xn with col_names false; [] for an empty file.

public function names(): array

Returns list<string>

CsvReader::next()

The next chunk of at most $rows rows in read_csv()’s shape, with the 1-based position of its first row and its row count; null once no rows remain. A chunk without rows comes only to carry problems found after the last row.

public function next(int $rows): ?array

Returns null\|array{position: int, rows: int, names: list<string>, columns: list<null\|array{type: 'bool'\|'int'\|'float'\|'string'\|'date'\|'datetime', values: list<bool\|int\|float\|string\|null>, failed: int}>, problems: list<string>}

Errors rows below 1, or a read error.
